tour.title: Start here: what this repository is and what it is not
tour.description: The repository holds ORISO-specific Keycloak material only: the realm reference (realm.json), the custom image source under keycloak-image/, helper scripts and the CI/release workflows. Runtime configuration and deployment belong to ORISO-Helm, not here. Read the README first, then DEPLOYMENT.md and STATUS.md for the cluster picture.

tour.title: The custom image: stock Keycloak plus the ORISO extension
tour.description: keycloak-image/Dockerfile builds the otp-config SPI (spi-build stage) and layers it, together with the ORISO theme, onto Keycloak. Stock Keycloak lacks the app-/email-authenticator, so every flow in the realm that mentions them only works with this image.

tour.title: Why 2FA lives here: the otp-config SPI
tour.description: ADR-013 puts second-factor logic into a vendored Keycloak extension instead of UserService. The SPI README and its OpenAPI file (keycloakextension.yaml) describe the contract UserService calls; the generated model classes in the SPI come from that file.

tour.title: The REST door: RealmOtpResourceProvider
tour.description: Registered as the realm resource 'otp-config', this class serves fetch-otp-setup-info, setup-otp, delete-otp, send-verification-mail and setup-otp-mail. It is the only place other services reach second-factor setup; ORISO-UserService calls it through IdentitySecondFactor and KeycloakService.

tour.title: Logging in with a code: the authenticators
tour.description: OtpMailAuthenticator (direct grant, id email-authenticator) and OtpMailFormAuthenticator (browser) send a code and check it in MailOtpVerifier; OtpAppAuthenticatorFactory covers app TOTP. OtpParameterAuthenticator reads the code from the request.

tour.title: The code itself: generation, lifetime and mail
tour.description: RandomDigitsCodeGenerator makes the digits, MemoryOtpService keeps code and expiry in memory (default lifetime 900 s) and OtpMailSender / DefaultMailSender deliver the mail. The mail credential is stored by MailOtpCredentialProvider and MailOtpCredentialService.

tour.title: Operating it: applying the flow and the e-mail theme
tour.description: Fresh realm imports get the 2FA direct-grant flow from realm.json; scripts/keycloak-apply-2fa-flow.sh applies it to an existing realm (idempotent, run in the pod of the oriso-keycloak image) and keycloak-verify-2fa-flow.sh checks it. sync-email-theme.sh copies the generated e-mail theme from ORISO-Frontend (ADR-020).

tour.title: Running in the cluster: deployment, HTTP mode and backups
tour.description: keycloak-deployment.yaml, keycloak-service.yaml and ingress.yaml describe the pod, service and route; configure-http-access.sh switches the realm to the internal HTTP mode behind TLS termination; backup/realm-backup.sh exports the realm from the running pod.
